findings.summary: Changed file outside the expected deliverables list
findings.evidence: `prediction_problem` was made `pub`, a one-line change, so the check can reuse the gate's rule. The file was on the planned-files list and is disclosed in the CHANGELOG, but it is not on the expected deliverables list.

findings.summary: Summary line under-counts the commits in the range
findings.evidence: The count is `report.commits.len()`, which includes only commits that could be classified. Run on the snapshot, it printed 'pr-head FAIL: 0 commit(s) between HEAD~1 and HEAD, 1 offending' even though the range holds 1 commit.

findings.summary: Content-match offence is skipped when other offences exist
findings.evidence: The head-content check runs only `if report.offences.is_empty()`. A head that has another offence and also a content mismatch will not report the mismatch. This is only a small gap against 'every offending commit is listed'.

findings.summary: No CLI-level test of the exit codes
findings.evidence: The exit-code behaviour (0 on pass, 2 on failure) is tested only through core tests and my manual run. No CLI integration test asserts it.

summary: The change adds `athena check --pr-head <base> <head>` and a `pr-head` CI job that runs on pull requests and does not block merging. The core logic is in the new `crates/athena-core/src/pr_check.rs`. It sorts each commit with `land::classify_commit`, the per-commit step taken out of `pr_commits` without changing what it does. It then checks that the verification passed, that the reading came first (the gate's `prediction_problem` rule), and that the head's content matches what the last landing verified. Every offending commit is listed by sha. I ran the 8 new tests and all passed. I also ran the CLI on the snapshot: it exited 2 and named the commit. It rejected `--history` combined with `--pr-head`. Athena's fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. All criteria are met. There are three minor findings. First, a one-line change in `athena-gate/src/invariant.rs` falls outside the deliverables list. It was planned and is needed to reuse the gate's rule. Second, the summary line counts only commits that could be classified, so it says "0 commit(s)" when there was one. Third, the content-match check runs only when there are no other offences.
